xebec: A small two-masted, and later three-masted, Mediterranean transport ship with an overhanging bow and stern.
xenia: The concept of hospitality to strangers.
xenial: Hospitable, especially to visiting strangers or foreigners.
xenic: Containing an unidentified organism, especially a bacterium.
xenodiagnosis: The diagnosis of an infectious disease (especially of trypanosomiasis) by exposure to a vector of that disease, incubating the vector and examining it for the presence of the di…
xenogamy: The transfer of pollen from the anthers of one plant to the stigma of another; cross-pollination.
xenogeneic: Derived from a different species and therefore genetically and immunologically incompatible
xenograft: A tissue graft taken from a species different from that of the recipient.
xenolith: Any piece of rock having a different origin to that of the igneous rock in which it is found.
xenolithic: Being or pertaining to a xenolith.
xenon: The chemical element (symbol Xe) with an atomic number of 54.
xenophile: A person who has a love of foreign people and culture.
xenophobe: One who hates or fears strangers or foreigners.
xenophobia: A fear, antipathy, or hatred of strangers or foreigners.
xenophobic: Exhibiting or characterised by xenophobia, a fear or hatred of strangers, foreigners, or extraterrestial life.
xenotropic: Describing a virus growing in tissue of an organism other than its normal host.
xeric: Very dry, lacking humidity and water.
xerographic: of, relating to, or produced by xerography
xerographically: In a xerographic way; by xerography.
xerography: A photocopying process in which a negative image formed on an electrically charged plate is transferred as a positive to paper and thermally fixed.
xerophilous: Able to thrive in dry weather.
xerophthalmia: A condition due to a deficiency of vitamin A where the conjunctiva and cornea become dry.
xerophyte: Any plant suited for life in a habitat where water is scarce, such as in a desert or chaparral.
xerophytic: Of, pertaining to, or being a xerophyte
xerophytism: The adaptation of plants to habitats where water is scarce.
xeroradiography: A method of X-ray photography which uses an electrically charged metal plate instead of film.
xerosere: The succession of ecological communities which originated in an extremely dry habitat such as a desert or sand dunes.
xeroxed: simple past and past participle of xerox
xeroxing: present participle and gerund of xerox
